dossier.purpose: Monorepo (Cargo workspace v1.7.0, LightOn, Apache-2.0) with two surfaces. (1) ColGREP (colgrep/): a local CLI for semantic + regex + keyword code search. It splits files into code units with tree-sitter, converts each to structured text, embeds it in-process with a local ONNX ColBERT model (default lightonai/LateOn-Code-edge, fetched from Hugging Face), and stores a multi-vector PLAID index plus SQLite/FTS5 metadata per (project path, model) under the user data dir (~/.local/share/colgrep/indices on Linux). Every search first incrementally updates that index. Documented agent integrations: Claude Code (plugin with hooks + skill), Codex (AGENTS.md section + sandbox writable_roots entry), OpenCode, Hermes, Kimi Code. ColGREP has no MCP server, daemon or HTTP mode and no pluggable remote embedding service. (2) NextPlaid (next-plaid/, next-plaid-onnx/, next-plaid-api/): the multi-vector index library, an ONNX ColBERT encoder crate, and an optional separate REST API server (Docker) with a Python client/CLI that can encode text server-side; ColGREP does not call that server.

claims.claim: ColGREP is 'Semantic code search for your terminal and your coding agents. Searches combine regex filtering with semantic ranking. All local, your code never leaves your machine.'

'No server, no API, no dependencies. ColGREP is a single Rust binary with everything baked in.' `colgrep init` builds the index; after that every search detects file changes and updates the index automatically before returning results.

Default model is lightonai/LateOn-Code-edge; any ColBERT-style HF model via `colgrep set-model` or `--model`; HF_TOKEN for private models. Each (project, model) pair has its own index directory so switching models never corrupts existing indexes; `colgrep clear` scopes to the active model, `clear --all` wipes every index.

Agent integrations table: Claude Code (`colgrep --install-claude-code`), OpenCode, Codex (`--install-codex`), Hermes; 'Claude Code has full hooks support. OpenCode, Codex, and Hermes integrations are basic for now'. colgrep/README.md also lists Kimi Code.

Pipeline: tree-sitter parse -> structured representation -> LateOn-Code-edge (17M, 'runs on CPU') multi-vector embeddings -> NextPlaid index (quantized, memory-mapped, incremental) -> grep-compatible search with SQLite filtering and semantic ranking, '100% local'.
Benchmark: NDCG@10 on the Semble public bench (1,251 queries x 63 repos x 19 languages, FP32, single H100): ColGREP LateOn-Code 0.859, semble potion-code-16M 0.853, ColGREP LateOn-Code-edge 0.846.

NextPlaid is 'A local-first multi-vector database with a REST API' with built-in ONNX encoding ('no external inference server needed'), memory-mapped indices, 2/4-bit quantization, incremental add/delete, SQLite metadata pre-filtering, CPU-optimized with optional CUDA.

Default query runs ColBERT semantic search plus 'FTS5 trigram keyword search' fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (alpha=0.75); -e regex pre-filters then semantics ranks; test functions are demoted unless the query mentions 'test'.

Indexes are stored outside the project (~/.local/share/colgrep/indices on Linux, ~/Library/Application Support/colgrep/indices on macOS; XDG_DATA_HOME honored); per-project dir {project}-{hash8} holds index/, state.json, project.json; 'ColGREP automatically detects and repairs index/metadata desync from interrupted operations.'

'macOS binaries ship with Apple Accelerate + CoreML'; 'Linux & Windows binaries work immediately but run on CPU only'; acceleration on Linux/Windows via `cargo install colgrep --features ...` (openblas, cuda, cuda+tensorrt, cuda-13, directml).

Claude Code integration installs session and task hooks that inject colgrep usage instructions, 'check index health before activating (skips if >3000 chunks need indexing or index is desynced)', and propagate instructions to spawned sub-agents.

ONNX Runtime is downloaded automatically on first use (lookup: ORT_DYLIB_PATH, Python envs, system paths, auto-download to ~/.cache/onnxruntime/); config is stored at ~/.config/colgrep/config.json (XDG_CONFIG_HOME overrides).

PRIVACY: source code never leaves the machine; 'single network request on first use' (model download from Hugging Face), then works offline; no telemetry/analytics/crash reports; indices stored in `.colgrep/` within the project directory.

NextPlaid API server (Docker ghcr.io/lightonai/next-plaid:cpu-1.7.0 / cuda-1.7.0) runs in two modes: with --model the server encodes text (*_with_encoding endpoints), without it clients send embeddings; async batched writes (202), optional rate limiting (off by default), Swagger UI, automatic index/SQLite sync repair.

install.method: Homebrew (README says macOS / Linux; the generated formula has an x86_64 Linux URL only)
Cargo from crates.io (default features = CPU only; optional --features accelerate,coreml | openblas | cuda | cuda,tensorrt | cuda-13)

install.method: Docker image of the optional NextPlaid API server (CPU; CUDA variant is ghcr.io/lightonai/next-plaid:cuda-1.7.0 with --gpus all)
pip, NextPlaid Python client (CLI extra: pip install next-plaid-client[cli])

readme.telemetry_and_network: Telemetry: none found in code (repo-wide grep for telemetry/analytics/sentry/posthog/opentelemetry hits only colgrep/PRIVACY.md:18-20, which states none is collected). ColGREP network use: (1) Hugging Face Hub model download on first use or model switch via hf-hub, using HF_TOKEN/HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN for private repos, default revision, no hash pinning (colgrep/src/model.rs:25-89); a local model directory path avoids it (model.rs:29-32). (2) ONNX Runtime 1.23.0 downloaded from github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime releases (NuGet for DirectML) on first use unless ORT_DYLIB_PATH or a cached/found copy exists, with no checksum/signature check in code (colgrep/src/onnx_runtime.rs:33, 126-155, 529-587, 603-623). (3) `colgrep update` queries github.com and pipes the installer into sh; user-invoked only, no automatic update check (colgrep/src/commands/update.rs:11-105, grep). (4) Subprocesses: git worktree list (index/worktree.rs:37-73), curl/sh/powershell (update.rs), the claude CLI (install/claude_code.rs:83-195). No account or API key is required (HF token only for private models); no code, queries or embeddings are sent anywhere (the only HTTP client in colgrep is ureq for the ORT download, plus hf-hub). PRIVACY.md:14-16 mentions only the model download and omits the ORT download. Optional NextPlaid API server (separate): no authentication, binds 0.0.0.0:8080 by default, CORS Any (next-plaid-api/src/main.rs:345-348, 521); its Docker entrypoint downloads models from huggingface.co with curl (next-plaid-api/docker-entrypoint.sh:50-67).

entry_points.what: `colgrep` binary (clap, cli.rs). Default `colgrep QUERY [PATH...]` plus subcommands search/init/status/clear/set-model/settings/update; global --install-*/--uninstall-*, --stats, --force-cpu/--force-gpu; hidden --session-hook/--task-hook used by the Claude Code plugin.
`colgrep` library crate re-exporting IndexBuilder, Searcher, IndexState, extract_units, ensure_model, ensure_onnx_runtime and the install_* functions (lines 8-48).

`next-plaid-api` axum REST server (hand-parsed args --host/--port/--index-dir/--model/--cuda/--int8/--parallel...; routers at lines 322-505; Swagger UI); Docker entry via next-plaid-api/docker-entrypoint.sh.
Python SDK (client.py sync, async_client.py, models.py, exceptions.py) and the `next-plaid` click CLI (cli.py; pyproject.toml:34-35).

`next_plaid_onnx::Colbert` ONNX Runtime ColBERT encoder (lib + cdylib; CPU/CUDA/TensorRT/CoreML/DirectML providers) with hierarchy.rs token pooling; Python export CLIs `pylate-onnx-export` / `colbert-quantize` in next-plaid-onnx/python/src/colbert_export/cli.py.
`next-plaid` core library: MmapIndex create/update/search/delete, ResidualCodec, SQLite `filtering`, FTS5 `text_search`, optional CUDA.

Agent installers called from main.rs: claude_code.rs, codex.rs, opencode.rs, hermes.rs, kimi.rs, uninstall.rs with embedded SKILL.md, hook.json, plugin.json, marketplace.json; repo root also carries a Claude plugin (.claude-plugin/, hooks/hook.json, skills/colgrep/SKILL.md).
`colgrep_parser` PyO3 extension (maturin; out-of-workspace crate): parse_code/detect_language/embedding-text only, no indexing or search.

code.architecture: Cargo workspace (Cargo.toml:1-3) of four crates. next-plaid = core multi-vector PLAID index (index.rs, search.rs, update.rs, delete.rs, codec.rs, kmeans.rs, maxsim.rs, mmap.rs; filtering.rs = SQLite metadata with whitelist-validated SQL conditions; text_search.rs = FTS5 + score fusion; binary.rs = 1-bit storage; cuda.rs). next-plaid-onnx = ONNX Runtime ColBERT encoder (src/lib.rs, hierarchy.rs pooling) + python/ export tooling. next-plaid-api = axum server (main.rs, handlers/{documents,search,encode,rerank,metadata}.rs, state.rs with ArcSwap index slots and batch queues). colgrep = CLI: main.rs/cli.rs -> commands/{search,init,status,clear,config,hooks,update,stats}.rs -> index/mod.rs (6.4k-line IndexBuilder/Searcher: scan_files honoring .gitignore + IGNORED_DIRS, tree-sitter parsers in parser/{extract,analysis,ast,call_graph,language}.rs + per-language files, embed.rs structured text, pooled ONNX encoding pipeline, PLAID write + SQLite/FTS5 metadata, content-hash/mtime/size update plan, resumable build with .building marker, dirty-flag repair, atomic full_rebuild via index.tmp/index.old) -> ranking.rs path penalties/boosts -> display.rs. State: index/paths.rs (data dir, {project}-{xxh3(path|model)[:8]} dir name, .lock file lock), index/state.rs (state.json: per-file hash/mtime/size, ignored_files, search_count, dirty, INDEX_FORMAT_VERSION=2), project.json (canonical path + model), index/worktree.rs (seed a new git worktree's index from a sibling), config.rs (config.json in the data dir's parent), model.rs (HF download), onnx_runtime.rs (locate/download libonnxruntime), acceleration.rs. Hybrid results are collapsed to one entry per file (index/mod.rs:4571-4580). No daemon or server: every query is a fresh process that loads the ONNX model.
code.packaging_and_release: cargo-dist 0.30.3 (Cargo.toml:37-39) autogenerated release.yml, triggered by version tags (release.yml:41-46), builds colgrep archives plus shell/powershell installers for aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-apple-darwin, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc (Cargo.toml:79-86); no Linux aarch64 binary. Per-target features are injected at build time (release.yml:157-183): macOS arm64 coreml+accelerate+metal_gpu, macOS x86_64 accelerate, Linux x86_64 mkl+cuda (CUDA toolkit 12.4 installed, release.yml:143-153), Windows directml. GitHub Release created with gh release create (release.yml:311-321). crates.io: next-plaid, next-plaid-onnx, colgrep published with `cargo publish --no-verify`, continue-on-error (release.yml:323-350). next-plaid-api is dist=false (next-plaid-api/Cargo.toml:9-10) and shipped as Docker images by a manual workflow_dispatch job (docker-release.yml:27-28, 93-104): ghcr.io/lightonai/next-plaid:{cpu,cuda}-<version> and -latest, cpu amd64+arm64, cuda amd64. Checksums: per-archive .sha256 files (update-homebrew-tap.yml:52-54); no signatures, attestations, SBOM or provenance steps in any workflow (grep). Actions are pinned to mutable tags (ci.yml:18-19); cargo-dist installed via curl|sh of a version-pinned URL (release.yml:68). Also present: flake.nix (x86_64-linux only, not documented in README, flake.nix:12) and prebuilt 0.1.0 wheels under next-plaid-api/python-sdk/dist/ and next-plaid-onnx/python/dist/ in the checkout.
code.tests_and_ci: Frameworks: Rust #[test]/#[tokio::test], pytest, criterion dev-dep in next-plaid. About 1,066 Rust test attributes (colgrep 762 in 56 files, next-plaid 216 in 23, next-plaid-api 48 in 7, next-plaid-onnx 40 in 2) and about 178 Python test functions (4 files). About 51 dedicated test files: colgrep/src/parser/tests/ (36 per-language test_*.rs + common.rs/mod.rs) and colgrep/src/parser/test_core.rs; next-plaid/tests/ (8); next-plaid-api/tests/ (integration_tests.rs, start_from_scratch_env_test.rs, test_api.py); next-plaid-api/python-sdk/tests/ (test_cli.py, test_integration.py); next-plaid-onnx/python/tests/test_cli.py. There is no colgrep/tests/ directory; index, state, lock, repair and config tests are inline #[cfg(test)] (colgrep/src/index/mod.rs alone has 75). CI (.github/workflows): ci.yml (push/PR to main: rustfmt, clippy -D warnings with openblas, cargo test --features openblas on ubuntu-latest and ubuntu-24.04-arm, cargo doc -D warnings, cargo bench --no-run, onnx crate test + clippy, colgrep fmt/test/clippy, Python SDK `pytest tests/test_cli.py` only); cli-e2e.yml (builds colgrep with mkl,cuda / accelerate,coreml,metal_gpu / directml on ubuntu/macos/windows and runs the real CLI on a sample project: index+search, --include, -l, -e, --json, status, clear, re-index, relative-path assertion; downloads the model from Hugging Face at test time); release.yml (cargo-dist plan on PRs, publish on tags); docker-release.yml (manual); update-homebrew-tap.yml; python-sdk-release.yml; docs.yml (docs/build_docs.py -> GitHub Pages). Live-server tests (test_api.py, SDK test_integration.py) run via scripts/run-api-tests.sh (Makefile:104-106), which no workflow invokes. No cargo-audit, cargo-deny, dependabot or CodeQL configuration found; no rust-version/rust-toolchain pin (CI uses stable).

code.security_policy: none - no SECURITY.md or vulnerability-reporting policy at the repo root, in .github/, or anywhere else (glob for SECURITY*). Only colgrep/PRIVACY.md exists (privacy statement, contact contact@lighton.ai at colgrep/PRIVACY.md:28).

claim_checks.claim: Index location: colgrep/README.md:592-602 says indexes live outside the project (~/.local/share/colgrep/indices on Linux, ~/Library/Application Support/colgrep/indices on macOS, XDG_DATA_HOME honored), while colgrep/PRIVACY.md:10 says they are stored in `.colgrep/` within the project directory.
claim_checks.evidence: Code agrees with the README and contradicts PRIVACY.md. get_colgrep_data_dir() = $COLGREP_DATA_DIR, else $XDG_DATA_HOME or the platform data dir, + colgrep/indices (colgrep/src/index/paths.rs:69-90); per-index dir = {sanitized project name}-{first 8 hex of xxh3_64(path|model)} (paths.rs:96-123); cli.rs:66 help says the same. The string '.colgrep' appears in no Rust source (grep). The index root is the canonical directory colgrep is run in, or an existing parent index (colgrep/src/commands/search.rs:1058-1078; paths.rs:182-226); there is no git-root detection (grep).

claim_checks.claim: README.md:63,75: each (project, model) pair has its own index; `colgrep set-model` keeps existing indexes for other models; `colgrep clear` is scoped to the active model and `clear --all` wipes everything. (colgrep/README.md:414 and cli.rs:53,147 instead say set-model 'clears existing indexes'.)

The 'clears existing indexes' wording in colgrep/README.md:414 and colgrep/src/cli.rs:53,147 is stale.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:49: after `colgrep init`, every search detects file changes and updates the index automatically before returning results.
claim_checks.evidence: search_single_path runs IndexBuilder::try_index before every search unless --no-update (colgrep/src/commands/search.rs:1103-1189; flag at cli.rs:457-459). try_index takes a non-blocking file lock; if another process holds it the search proceeds on the existing index (colgrep/src/index/mod.rs:1813-1823; search.rs:1142-1149) and a failed load is retried 3 times (search.rs:1232-1264). Change detection uses stored content hash + mtime(ns) + size (index/state.rs:75-99; mod.rs:4778-4799). 'Corrupted' load errors delete that index dir and rebuild it (search.rs:1157-1170, 1266-1309). A first build above 30,000 code units prompts only on a TTY (index/mod.rs:458, 4745-4747).

claim_checks.claim: colgrep/README.md:608: 'ColGREP automatically detects and repairs index/metadata desync from interrupted operations.'
claim_checks.evidence: state.json is written atomically via temp file + rename (colgrep/src/index/state.rs:122-149); a `dirty` flag is set before writes (index/mod.rs:2635-2638) and repair_index_db_sync trims orphan index docs / DB rows (mod.rs:1607-1662, 2579-2585); first builds are resumable with a `.building` marker and checkpoints every ~4,096 units (mod.rs:52-57, 2141-2208); full rebuilds go to index.tmp and are swapped in atomically with index.old rollback (mod.rs:2429-2540); a missing state.json is reconstructed from the SQLite DB and count mismatches are reconciled (mod.rs:1760-1805); an INDEX_FORMAT_VERSION mismatch (currently 2) forces one rebuild (state.rs:47-51; mod.rs:1706-1723); a .lock file serializes writers with a 5 s wait (paths.rs:243-288). `colgrep status` only prints project/model/index path (commands/status.rs:36-44), no health report.

claim_checks.claim: README.md:49 'No server, no API, no dependencies... single Rust binary with everything baked in' and colgrep/PRIVACY.md:14-16 'single network request on first use' (model download), no other requests.

PRIVACY.md omits the ORT download; `colgrep update` also contacts github.com (commands/update.rs:11-105, user-invoked). No telemetry/analytics code found (grep).

claim_checks.evidence: Code differs from the README: the FTS index is built with FtsTokenizer::IdentifierAware, not trigram (colgrep/src/index/mod.rs:889-894, 4297-4306); fusion is fuse_relative_score, a min-max score fusion whose comment says it beats rank-RRF (mod.rs:4458-4485); default alpha is 0.60 (colgrep/src/config.rs:463-480, COLGREP_ALPHA env override; cli.rs:735 and config.rs:173 still say 0.75, cli.rs:389 says 0.60). Afterwards it applies path-noise penalties to test/compat/example paths unless the query contains 'test', 'spec' or 'benchmark' (colgrep/src/ranking.rs:122-140, 161-164) plus path-stem, definition and file-coherence boosts and one-result-per-file collapsing (index/mod.rs:4491-4580). --semantic-only (search_with_embedding, mod.rs:4336-4364) applies none of these.

claim_checks.claim: colgrep/README.md:438-444: the Claude Code integration installs session and task hooks that inject usage instructions, 'check index health before activating (skips if >3000 chunks need indexing or index is desynced)' and propagate instructions to sub-agents.

risks: Integration is shell-out only and has start-up cost: no MCP server, daemon or HTTP mode in ColGREP (no 'mcp' anywhere in the repo; no listener in colgrep/src), so Claude Code and Codex are only told via hook/AGENTS.md text to run `colgrep` (colgrep/src/commands/hooks.rs:54-104; colgrep/src/install/codex.rs:149-183). Every query is a fresh process that loads the ONNX model; the hook text itself warns the first query 'may take 30-90 seconds' (hooks.rs:93-94). A first index above 30,000 code units prompts on a TTY but auto-confirms when stdin is not a TTY (colgrep/src/index/mod.rs:458, 4745-4747).

No remote or pluggable embedding service: embeddings are computed in-process by a local ONNX ColBERT export with tokenizer.json/onnx_config.json etc. (colgrep/src/model.rs:7-19, 25-89; next-plaid-onnx/Cargo.toml:35). The only HTTP embedding endpoint in the repo is NextPlaid API's ColBERT-specific /encode (next-plaid-api/src/main.rs:376-398), which colgrep never calls (colgrep/Cargo.toml:17-20; its only network code is ureq for ORT at onnx_runtime.rs:576 and hf-hub at model.rs:38-65); no OpenAI-compatible route exists (repo-wide grep).

First-use supply chain: ONNX Runtime 1.23.0 is downloaded from github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime (NuGet for DirectML) with no checksum or signature check (colgrep/src/onnx_runtime.rs:529-587, 603-623) and model weights come from the Hugging Face default revision with no pinned revision or hash (colgrep/src/model.rs:38-65, 47). The documented installer and `colgrep update` pipe a remote script to sh (README.md:33; colgrep/src/commands/update.rs:82-91). Offline use needs a pre-seeded ORT_DYLIB_PATH and a local model directory (onnx_runtime.rs:126-142; model.rs:29-32); CUDA-feature builds, which include the Linux prebuilt, skip local ORT discovery entirely (onnx_runtime.rs:144-155).

Documentation drift: code differs from README/CLI help/PRIVACY on index location (PRIVACY.md:10 says .colgrep/ in the project; code uses the user data dir, colgrep/src/index/paths.rs:83-90), config path (docs say ~/.config/colgrep/config.json and XDG_CONFIG_HOME; code writes <data dir parent>/config.json and never reads XDG_CONFIG_HOME, colgrep/src/config.rs:588-595), keyword tokenizer/fusion/alpha (docs: trigram + RRF + 0.75; code: IdentifierAware + relative-score + 0.60, index/mod.rs:889-894, 4458-4485, config.rs:463-480), set-model (docs: clears indexes; code keeps them, colgrep/src/commands/config.rs:78-89), default path style (docs: absolute; code: relative, config.rs:414-418 and cli-e2e.yml:380-398), large-index prompt (docs: >10K units; code: 30,000, index/mod.rs:458), hook health check (README only, hooks.rs:8-25), Linux 'CPU only' (release builds with cuda, release.yml:168-169), ONNX Runtime cache dir and lookup (code: ~/.cache/colgrep/onnxruntime/<ver>/<cpu|gpu>, no system-path probing on Linux, onnx_runtime.rs:517-537), language count (README 35 code languages; Language enum has 46 variants, parser/types.rs:7-58; cli.rs:292 says 18+). Behavior must be confirmed against the binary rather than the docs.

Agent-environment coupling: indexes live outside the workspace, so Codex's default workspace-write sandbox blocks index writes unless `--install-codex` adds ~/.local/share/colgrep/indices to [sandbox_workspace_write].writable_roots in ~/.codex/config.toml (colgrep/src/install/codex.rs:36-47, 229-245) - a widening of sandbox write access whose path is fixed at install time from XDG_DATA_HOME/COLGREP_DATA_DIR (paths.rs:69-90). Installers hard-code ~/.codex and ~/.claude/settings.json (codex.rs:19-22; claude_code.rs:197-201; no CODEX_HOME/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR support, grep), need claude CLI >= 2.0.36 (claude_code.rs:16), and the hooks/AGENTS.md text instruct the model to use colgrep instead of Grep/Glob and never fall back to grep (hooks.rs:70, 96; skills/colgrep/SKILL.md:5).

Index lifecycle and scoping limits: the index root is the canonical directory where colgrep is first run (no git-root detection) and the directory name hashes path|model (colgrep/src/index/paths.rs:92-123), so moving/renaming a repo or switching model builds a new full index; nothing garbage-collects old ones except `colgrep clear --all` (commands/clear.rs:17-55). The default ignore list skips directories named bin, out, external, logs, tmp, temp, vendor, build, dist and others (index/mod.rs:3066-3128), files over 512 KB are skipped (mod.rs:42) and embedded text is truncated at 8 KB (embed.rs:9). A load error that looks like corruption deletes and rebuilds the whole index dir (commands/search.rs:1163-1170, 1282-1308). --binary storage disables incremental updates (colgrep/README.md:331-335; index/mod.rs:2565-2577).

Security posture: no SECURITY.md or vulnerability-reporting policy; release assets carry .sha256 files but no signatures, attestations or SBOM, and no dependency scanning (cargo-audit/deny, dependabot, CodeQL) is configured (workflow grep); GitHub Actions are pinned to mutable tags (ci.yml:18-19; python-sdk-release.yml:31). The optional NextPlaid API server has no authentication, binds 0.0.0.0:8080 by default, uses CORS Any and accepts client-supplied SQL WHERE conditions (whitelist-validated) (next-plaid-api/src/main.rs:345-348, 521; next-plaid/README.md:367); the README compose files publish port 8080 on all interfaces (next-plaid-api/README.md:590-591); the Docker image runs as non-root uid 1000 (next-plaid-api/Dockerfile:198, 218).

Maintenance, licensing and evidence quality: ort is pinned to the pre-release =2.0.0-rc.11 (next-plaid-onnx/Cargo.toml:35); no MSRV or toolchain pin (CI uses stable); stale metadata such as .claude-plugin/plugin.json version 1.1.1 vs 1.7.0 (Makefile:236-241 bump-version omits it); the Linux release binary statically links Intel MKL through the mkl feature (release.yml:169; next-plaid/Cargo.toml:23) while the repo ships only the Apache-2.0 LICENSE with no NOTICE/third-party license file, and model licenses live on Hugging Face, not in the repo. All published quality numbers are author-reported (FP32 on H100) while the default CPU configuration is INT8 (colgrep/src/config.rs:279-288), and ranking constants were tuned on the same Semble benchmark (config.rs:463-470; ranking.rs:19-20).
